# Two arms

## When it applies
Whenever both arms take part: one works while the other holds or watches, an object passes between them, or they carry something together.

## How
Give each arm a role: working, holding, or watching. An arm that holds or supports something must stay still while the other works on it, and must not also serve as your viewpoint. Hands apart does not mean arms apart: think of whole arms and loads, and move the idle arm out of the way first. Where both need one region, finish, release and withdraw one before the other enters. Passing crossing paths with loads: one waits at a safe spot while the other goes.

To pass an object: set it down at a spot both arms reach and let the other arm pick it up, which is the simple way, or hand it over in the air with the receiving arm gripping a part the giver leaves free, and the giver opening only once the receiver's reading shows it holds. To carry something together, grip it with both before lifting, and move both hands the same way.

## Checks
Never release on hope.

## Recovery
robo.both and every free motion check the two arms against each other and refuse if they would meet; when the hands are meant to work close together, pass force=True.
